items.title: Smashing Pumpkins Share New Butch Vig-Produced Song “Black Stars” for Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping: Stream
items.summary:
The Smashing Pumpkins have released "Black Stars," a new song recorded for the soundtrack of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, the prequel film arriving November 20th. The track is the band's first recorded with producer Butch Vig in 33 years.

Vig produced and engineered the Pumpkins' 1991 debut Gish and returned for 1993's Siamese Dream before the band moved on to other collaborators, chiefly Flood and Alan Moulder on 1995's Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness. The reunion had been teased months in advance: as Consequence reported, Billy Corgan said during a Substack livestream back in May that the band had cut a song with Vig behind the board and that it was 98 percent finished. "Black Stars" turned out to be that song.

Musically it lands in moody mid-tempo territory, built on a siren-like guitar figure, layered vocal harmonies, a half-time bridge and Corgan's familiar sneer. An official video accompanies the release.

The band is currently on the road with the Rats in a Cage Tour, a North American arena run that features a full performance of Mellon Collie alongside a selection of other hits. Remaining dates include Jacksonville and Tampa on October 17th and 18th, Denver on October 27th, Las Vegas on October 30th, Vancouver on November 5th and the Kia Forum in Inglewood on November 12th, with the Darker Waves festival in Huntington Beach on November 14th closing the leg.

Corgan also contributed to Consequence's list of the 100 Best Bands of All Time, where he singled out the Kinks alongside the Beatles, the Rolling Stones and the Who. "Ray [Davies] is one of the greatest songwriters of all time," he said. "They opened up genres that didn't exist."

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan Compete on David Byrne’s Gameshow in “Expectations” Video
items.summary:
Olivia Rodrigo has enlisted Chappell Roan for a remix of "Expectations," a song from her new album You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, and the two have released a music video to go with it. In the clip, Rodrigo and Roan appear as contestants on a game show hosted by David Byrne, a vocal Rodrigo fan. Producer Dan Nigro, who has worked with both singers, turns up as well.

The pairing has history. Roan opened for Rodrigo on tour, a run that helped push her from a long stretch as a working songwriter toward mainstream attention in 2024, alongside a string of widely shared festival sets.

Rodrigo is on the road now with the Unraveled Tour behind You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, her third studio album and the follow-up to 2023's Guts. The record includes "The Cure," "Serena Joy" and "What's Wrong With Me," a duet with Robert Smith. Pitchfork, which detailed the album's making in a cover story by Shaad D'Souza, also noted that Rodrigo organized the first Daisy Chain Fields, a charity festival built around a lineup celebrating womanhood.

Roan, meanwhile, released her debut The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess in 2023 and won Best New Artist at the 2025 Grammy Awards. She followed the album with the single "The Giver" and later "The Subway," which earned her two nominations at this year's ceremony.

Next week Roan hosts a charity concert billed as The Super Graphic Spectacular, with Caroline Polachek, Tinashe and MUNA among the performers.

items.title: The Pretty Reckless Unveil New Version of “About You” Featuring Dave Grohl and Pat Smear: Stream
items.summary:
The Pretty Reckless have released a new version of "About You" featuring Foo Fighters members Dave Grohl and Pat Smear. Grohl plays drums and sings on the bonus rendition, with Smear on guitar.

"About You" first appeared on Dear God, the band's most recent album, released in June. The reworked take leans power-pop, with Taylor Momsen singing the verses and Grohl joining on the chorus before the two trade call-and-response vocals in the bridge.

Momsen described the collaboration as a deliberate choice rather than a happy accident. "'About You' is one of my favorite songs on the record, so I wanted to do something special," she said in comments reported by Consequence. "I called Dave and Pat and asked them if they'd lend their magic to it. It was an amazing time in the studio making music, there's nothing better than jamming with friends. I couldn't be happier with the result."

The two camps have been circling each other for months. The Pretty Reckless recently finished a tour supporting AC/DC and had to miss two dates because of scheduling conflicts; Foo Fighters stepped in, and Grohl joined AC/DC onstage for "Highway to Hell" at the tour's final show at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

The Pretty Reckless begin a UK and European tour next month, then support Foo Fighters at two shows in India in late January. Foo Fighters head to Australia in November and South America in February.
